To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the urinary NGAL levels were significantly higher in patients with CIAKI than in those without CIAKI; 2) the urinary NGAl level was a significant and independent predictor of CIAKI; 3) the urinary NGA1 level in the early post contrast phase was a powerful independent predictor of subsequent development of CIAKI; and 4) the urinary NGal level was significantly higher in the patients with a higher risk of CIAKI than in the patients with lower risk

urinary neutrophil Gelatinase Associated Lipocalin (NGA) is a novel and useful biomarker in the diagnosis of CIAKI, and the prophylactic strategies are the most effective way to reduce the incidence of CIAKI.
the urinary NGAL levels may be used as a biomarker in CIAKI, and the reno protective strategies may prevent CIAKI.

the development of a novel biomarkers and reno protective strategies for CIAKI.
the pathogenesis of CIAKI, the identification of populations at high risk, the predictive factors of CIAKI and the treatment of such patients based on prophylaxis.
the development and evaluation of new biomarkers for the early detection of acute kidney injury and the identification of new targets for treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevention of CIAKI is a major concern for the clinician, and the usage of a biomarker for the detection of CIAKI in an early phase would be a promising tool for the future.
the early phase of CIAKI is associated with the increase of urinary NGAL, and the prevention of CIAKI is possible with the usage of small volume of iodinated contrast agent.
the early detection of the CIAKI by the novel urinary biomarker and the prophylactic strategies would reduce the incidence of the CIAKI.

the urinary NGAL may be a useful biomarker for the early detection of contrast induced nephropathy.

the urinary NGAL is a useful biomarker of the early phase of CIAKI.
